what: The JSON Formatter takes JSON text and makes it easy to read, checks that it is valid, or squeezes it into one compact line. JSON is the text format most websites, apps and APIs use to send data, but it often arrives as one long, unreadable line.

It helps developers, testers, students and anyone who has to look at an API response, a settings file or an exported data file. Use it when you need to read nested data, find a typing mistake, or make a file smaller before you paste it somewhere.
All checking and formatting happens in your browser, so your data is never uploaded.
uses: Paste a long one-line response from an API and click “Format” to see every key and value on its own line.
If a config file will not load, paste it here. The error message tells you what is wrong and near which position.
Click “Minify” to remove all spaces and line breaks before you put JSON into a URL, a database field or a test.
Validate JSON you wrote by hand before you send it to an API, so you do not get a confusing server error.
Clean up package.json, tsconfig.json or other config files so they are indented the same way everywhere.
tutorial: Click in the large “JSON” box and paste your text. It can be one line or many lines. Spaces at the start and end are ignored.
Click “Format” to rewrite the JSON with line breaks and an indent of 2 spaces. The result replaces the text in the same box.

Under the buttons you will see “Valid JSON.” in green if the text is correct. If it is not, you see “Invalid JSON:” followed by the browser’s explanation, which usually includes a position, line or column.
Use the position in the message to find the problem, fix it in the box, and click “Format” again. Repeat until you see “Valid JSON.”.
Click “Minify” if you need one line
“Minify” checks the JSON the same way, then removes every unneeded space and line break so the whole thing is on one line.
Click “Copy” to copy everything in the box to your clipboard, ready to paste into your editor or app.
Click “Clear” to empty the box and remove the message before you paste new JSON.
features: Nested objects and arrays are placed on separate lines with a 2-space indent, the most common style.
Produces the shortest valid version of your JSON on a single line.
Numbers keep every digit as you typed them, even very long IDs like 12345678901234567890 or values like 1.10, and repeated keys are not removed. Only the spaces and line breaks change.
Both buttons check the JSON first. You always know if it is valid before you use it.
When parsing fails, the message from the browser names the problem, with the line and column where it happened.
The output appears in the same box, so you can fix a value and format again without moving text around.
The “Copy” button copies the whole result at once, even when it is very long.

example.title: Worked example: formatting a small user record
example.text: Paste this one line into the box: {"name":"Asha","age":29,"skills":["js","css"],"active":true}. Click “Format”. The box now shows 9 lines: the opening brace, then "name": "Asha", "age": 29, a "skills" array with "js" and "css" each on its own line, "active": true, and the closing brace. The message says “Valid JSON.”. Now change the text to {"name":"Asha","age":29,} and click “Format” again. In Chrome you see “Invalid JSON: Expected double-quoted property name in JSON at position 24 (line 1 column 25)”, which points to the extra comma before the closing brace.

tips: Click “Format” on any JSON you receive before reading it. Nested data is much easier to follow with indentation.
The error message gives the line and column of the problem. Use them to jump close to the mistake.
Different browsers word the error message differently, but the position is usually close to the real problem.
If you only want to check that JSON is valid, click “Format” and read the message. You do not need to keep the output.
Click “Minify” and then “Copy” when you need JSON in a single line, for example inside a command-line argument.
problems: The message says “Paste some JSON first.”
The box is empty or contains only spaces. Paste your JSON and click the button again.
The error points to a place that looks fine
The real mistake is often just before that position, such as a missing comma, a missing closing quote or an extra comma at the end of a list.
JSON is stricter than JavaScript. Every key and every text value needs double quotes, and comments are not allowed. Remove comments and change single quotes to double quotes.
The output has 2 spaces but I need 4 or tabs
The tool always uses a 2-space indent. Use your code editor’s format command if your project needs a different indent.
